unmet in every particular, and cheaper now than when it was written. regularity is declared at betti.m2:244 with Options => {Weights => null} only -- no Strategy, no Algorithm, no addHook or runHooks anywhere for it -- and the real methods live in Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:640-654, where regularity Ideal, Module and Complex all go through betti(freeResolution ...) with no dispatch point. The package the file names exists, packages/Regularity.m2, but exports mRegularity, CM, MonCurve (:22): a parallel function, so a user who writes regularity I cannot reach its algorithm, and the package's own tests assert the two agree by hand, 'assert(mRegularity(I, MonCurve => true) == regularity I)'. The consequence is still accumulating: #4191, an open PR, adds weightedRegularity to Depth.m2 as a third name for a related computation. What has changed in the file's favour is that hookified methods are now M2's conventional pattern -- freeResolution, pushForward, minimalPrimes and kernel all dispatch this way -- so the mechanism is standard rather than novel, and the file's second clause, 'the value of Strategy should be checked, somehow', is what runHooks provides. #3321 (closed) is regularity over quotient rings, unrelated. Searched cache and gh search issues; nothing on hookifying regularity

the proposed model is dead and the need is met several times over. Reinteract (fishsoup.net/software/reinteract, Owen Taylor) has had no release since around 2010. What the file wanted from it -- tab completion, tooltips with information about what is on screen, inline graphs, portable to Windows and Mac -- is what the Jupyter notebook interface provides, and #605 'Jupyter interface' was closed 2025-10-02; Jupyter is a symbol in Core (changes.m2:1246). The wiki carries Using-Macaulay2-with-Jupyter, -with-VSCode, -with-Sublime, -with-Org-Mode and -with-Emacs pages plus Interfaces-to-Macaulay2, so there are now several, and Macaulay2Web is a browser front end besides. #675 (vim) is the other closed interface issue

both halves met, measured against the file's own numbers. It complains that replacing 80100 times in a 5643739-byte cedict is 'too slow, compared to emacs'; on a corpus of the same shape and size (5286599 bytes, 80100 lines, all 80100 substitutions firing -- output grew 881100 bytes) the file's own pattern runs in 0.246 s, against sed -E at 0.26 s and python3 re.sub at 0.214 s on the same file. #1425 'Switch to Boost::regex' (390894fe9f, 2020-07-26) is the change. 'Also, make it interruptable' is met too: alarm 1 during a 2.1-second replace over a 42 MB corpus interrupts it. Boost adds a bound of its own -- a catastrophic pattern like (a+)+b raises 'The complexity of matching the regular expression exceeded predefined bounds ... to prevent eternal matches' -- so a runaway match cannot happen either. #3513 and #332 are the live replace issues, about linear algebra speed and unicode

reproduces, and the finding is broader than the file's. Finding the ring shape took three tries: the file's F() returns a plain quotient coefficient ring, since with GF or toField the coefficient generator is not reachable at all and R_2 is 'index 2 out of bounds 0 .. 1'. With zzF = () -> (k0 := ZZ/2[ww]; k0/(k0_0^2+k0_0+1)), R = zzF()[x,y] and S = zzF()[x,y]: R_2 and S_2 are both ww, I = ideal(x+ww), and sub(I, {R_2 => S_2}) errors. The message has changed since 2009 -- 'expected substitution values and omitted generators to be in compatible rings' where the file has 'expected ww to be a generator of R' -- and it is not specific to the coefficient generator: sub(I, {R_0 => S_0}) fails identically, while (map(S,R)) I returns ideal(x+ww). So any partial substitution between two separately-constructed but identical rings fails, and the full ring map shows the answer is computable. The error is arguably honest, since with y omitted the result's ring is ambiguous between R and S, but the same shape is accepted when R and S are the same ring, which makes the failure look incidental. Searched cache and gh search issues: #1224 is QQ[a,a,a], replicated names within one ring; #1011 is a doc request that M2 does not enforce well-definedness; #1183 is GaloisField coefficient rings, the shape that here errors on R_2 instead. The maintainer's unpushed PR_ring-maps work is about which conversions are canonical, a different axis

three asks. The identity predicate is met: RingMap == ZZ at ringmap.m2:30-32, where f == 1 is 'source f === target f and f === id_(source f)'. The dispatch ask is unmet and is the same missed predicate as #4579, filed from this catalog out of 1-flattenRing-can-save-time, whose second half is that applying a ring map never short-circuits when f == 1 -- here it is composing rather than applying. RingMap * RingMap (ringmap.m2:383-397) unconditionally computes g matrix f, builds a fresh rawRingMap and constructs a new RingMap; over QQ[a..h], 200 compositions take 0.021s for f*zzid and 0.0205s for zzid*f against 0.035s for f*f, so cheaper but not free. Probe trap worth keeping: === on RingMaps is structural, so f*zzid === f is true and f.RawRingMap === g.RawRingMap is true, and neither shows a short-circuit -- what does is a marker in the cache, f.cache#"zzmarker" = 1 being invisible from (f*zzid).cache, proving a distinct object. The third ask, Schubert2 doing all pullbacks by ring maps to optimise composition on cycle classes, depends on the composition short-circuit existing first and is a package refactor. Commented on #4579 with the composition timings and the === trap. #1919 (RingMap.cache.DegreeMap) and #1518 (kernels over ZZ) are the other open RingMap items, neither this

the premise is gone: M2 no longer builds rpms, so there is no *.spec file whose %dir entries could be missing. beeb464469 (2025-09-13) removed the --enable-rpm configure option and 6c833cbf0c (2025-09-08) the Debian packaging directory, both by the maintainer who now packages M2 downstream; M2/distributions/ holds only freebsd, install, tar and top. The report itself is a 2008 email from a Warwick user about RedHat rpms on Dan's own download site leaving empty directory trees behind after removal, and Dan's guess that not listing directory names in the spec file explained it. Same seam as 1-porting, 1-opensuse-build-service and 1-rpm-repository. #60, #240 and #678 are the surviving rpm issues, all closed and all about building rather than about spec-file directory ownership

same seam as its sibling 1-rpm-directories-linger, and dead for the same reason: M2 stopped shipping rpms (beeb464469 removed --enable-rpm, 2025-09-13), so there is no set of rpms for createrepo to index. The file is six lines noting that createrepo had moved from linux.duke.edu to createrepo.baseurl.org and recording the invocation; createrepo itself was superseded by createrepo_c years ago. Distribution repositories for M2 are now the distributions' own concern, which is the arrangement #4528 from this catalog serves by making configure report what it found for packagers

the need was met by a better mechanism than the one proposed. The file wants examples run by forking a warm process and redirecting i/o, for which it says M2 would need close ZZ, open String and dup2(ZZ,ZZ) -- none of which exists. Instead M2 grew capture (examples.m2:59-62, capture = method(Options => {UserMode => true, PackageExports => null}) over the built-in capture'), which runs an example in the *current* process with output collected, so there is no fork, no file-descriptor juggling and no startup cost at all -- strictly better than the proposal for the purpose stated. It is the default path: captureTestResult calls isCapturable and prefers capturing, falling back to a subprocess only when the example is not capturable (examples.m2:147 lists the exclusions, e.g. anything matching temporaryFileName). No single fix commit is identifiable; capture predates 2008 in some form and the method wrapper is later

unmet, and the remedy has become less applicable rather than more. Nothing in examples.m2 or testing.m2 sets up an unwritable directory -- no chmod, no fileMode -- so a package that writes stray files into the current directory still does so unnoticed. But capture (examples.m2:59-62), which is now the default path for running examples and which settled the sibling row 1-running-examples, runs them in M2's own process, so there is no per-example working directory whose permissions could be changed; doing it to M2's cwd would affect the whole run. M2 already has a blunter form of the idea in the --read-only-files command-line option, which refuses output files globally (stdio.d). The concern is real and acknowledged in passing: examples.m2:147 excludes from capture anything matching temporaryFileName, commented 'this is sometimes bug prone', so examples that make files are already a special case, by exclusion rather than prevention. If revisited, the plausible shape today is running check with cwd set somewhere disposable and diffing it afterwards, rather than an unwritable directory. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues; #1217 'Running M2 as root' is the only permissions-adjacent open item

does exactly what the file proposes. For R = QQ[x], S = R[y], f = map(R^2,R^2,matrix{{x,0},{0,1}}) and b = y_S, b*f returns a matrix over S with target and source S^2, and target(b*f) == S ** target f is true; entries are {{x*y,0},{0,y}}, so the R-entries are promoted and scaled. The mechanism is toSameRing (matrix.m2:13-21), called by RingElement * Matrix at :98-100, which promotes whichever side is promotable into the other's ring via isPromotable and errors otherwise. The file's condition that the modules be free is not needed for this to work. 0a494d5f6e (2009-01-24) is where toSameRing appears, its message including 'improve tensor product coercion', and 7a3be96374 and c969a5299c (2024) extended promotion for tensor products; the file is undated in the tree but the google-group exchange it cites puts it around then. #3906 'Constant times matrix fail' is the closed tracker version of the same area

unmet as asked, and the need has a shorter spelling than the proposal. Both transcripts still error identically: scan(5,9,identity) and apply(5,9,identity) give 'expected argument 1 to be a list or sequence'. But apply(5..8, identity) is (5,6,7,8), and .. is how ranges are written throughout M2 -- including the ..< operator this catalog settled as fixed in the previous batch, added at Mike's request in b8246778dd. The overload also carries a real cost: apply(5,f) iterates 0..4, so the first argument would mean 'count' at arity two and 'start' at arity three. The live requests in this family are about what the function may do rather than how the range is given -- #3870 'apply/scan should accept continue' and #4184 'try modifier in apply,select,etc', both open -- and nothing has asked for the two-integer form in seventeen years. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues

the shebang works. Wrote the file's own two lines -- '#! /usr/bin/M2 --script' then 'print a' -- made it executable and ran it: it executes, and scriptCommandLine is {./foo}. The file's transcript instead shows M2 failing to find ./foo, looking for it in the d/ source directory, which is what a build-tree M2 with an unset prefix would do. Handling is at startup.m2.in:534-546: commandLine#1 == "--script" takes commandLine#2 as the file and puts the rest in scriptCommandLine, with :464 erroring if --script is not first, which is what a shebang guarantees. No fix commit identified -- the failure looks like a 1.2-era build-tree path problem rather than a defect in the option. #234 'M2 --script' is open and about the option's design, not this

the system the file says is needed exists. about (help.m2:658, options {Body => false}) searches the installed documentation databases and returns numbered hits across all packages -- about "kernel" lists nodes from Complexes, CpMackeyFunctors and so on -- with Body => true to search node text rather than just keys; apropos (help.m2:639) matches symbol names; help and viewHelp do direct lookup. #774 'master documentation index and search function' is closed and is the tracker's version of this same request. The second sentence, 'Boolean operators in search expressions would be good, too', is half-served rather than met: about takes a regular expression, so alternation gives OR (about "kernel|cokernel"), while AND has no spelling and would need filtering two searches. Left unfiled because the live requests in this area already point at improving search rather than providing it -- #4324 'apropos with fuzzy search' and #4509 'Documentation nodes should be able to declare search aliases', the latter filed from this catalog out of 0-doc-Keywords, whose note records a single term returning 131 hits, which is the case where AND would actually help

select is a method function and users can add methods to it, which is the whole ask. class select is MethodFunctionWithOptions with eleven methods installed: (select,Thing,Function), (select,BasicList,Function), (select,BasicList,Type), (select,HashTable,Function), (select,Set,Function), (select,String,String), (select,String,String,String), (select,ZZ,Function), (select,ZZ,BasicList,Function), (select,ZZ,HashTable,Function), (select,ZZ,Set,Function). 3dc3352f44 (2020-07-28, #1425) 'allow select to have options, so the regex parameters can be adjusted' is the commit that gave it options; it was already a method by then. #578 and #579, both closed, are about what select means on Sets and HashTables rather than about its dispatch

the useful third of the file was taken into Core; the package it asks for was not, and nothing has asked for one since. recipN at hilbert.m2:12-26 is the file's recip1 verbatim, comments word for word ('n is a positive integer', 'g always has the form 1 plus terms weight 1,2,...,m-1', '1-f*g always has terms of wt m and higher'), sitting under '-- Local utilities', declared with := so file-local, beside a truncatePower helper and used by the Hilbert series machinery at :42 -- so the algorithm runs on every hilbertSeries call but only as private plumbing for that one caller. recip2 (constant unit) and recip (unit times an invertible monomial, using weightRange and exponents for the Laurent case) have no counterpart, and those are precisely the general cases a series package would need. No such package exists; PlaneCurveLinearSeries, SymbolicPowers and QthPower are unrelated. Not filed because a 'write a package' issue with no consumer sits indefinitely -- the README records that shape as why the wishlist files survived twenty-five years -- and the two open series issues would not be closed by it: #974 'Can't take value of a Hilbert series' and #598 'Defect in differentiation of Laurent series' each want a specific fix. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for series expansion, power series, recipN, truncatePower

the ask is unmet but the need is met, via debug Core, which the maintainer pointed out. setRandomSeed returns the NEW seed, not the previous one, because system.m2:146-148 ends with the assignment 'randomSeed = seed' (commented 'magic assignment, calls rawSetRandomSeed internally'), and randomSeed is not exported -- class randomSeed at top level is Symbol and it is absent from exports.m2. But debug Core is the supported route to private symbols and the round trip works: old = randomSeed (117061313407862), setRandomSeed 12345, setRandomSeed old, back to 117061313407862. It is also less private than the export status suggests, since setRandomSeed-doc.m2:17 names it -- 'Otherwise sets randomSeed to a value based on seed' -- so a reader is told the variable exists, though it has no node of its own. Core does the same save/restore internally with pushvar(symbol randomSeed, ...) and popvar at examples.m2:75 and :122. What remains is ergonomics: debug Core puts Core's whole private dictionary on dictionaryPath to read one integer, with the shadowing costs several rows in this catalog are about -- a cost of debug Core generally rather than of this feature. Changing setRandomSeed's return value would also break callers relying on the present one. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for setRandomSeed, randomSeed, previous seed, restore seed: #89, #3800, #978, all closed and about randomness in tests

a latent hazard in Core-private code, with the file's own instance gone and no reachable case found. buildPrefix, which the file calls 'exactly the situation', is no longer anywhere in m2/. The mechanism it wished for -- 'Dynamic scoping, as in lisp, has its uses!' -- was built as pushvar/popvar (Core.m2:67-73) and is used at eight sites: inDebugger (code.m2:282), randomSeed and OutputDictionary (examples.m2:75,86), printWidth (format.m2:317 and installPackage.m2:381), currentPackage (installPackage.m2:696), flagInhomogeneity (modules2.m2:136). It does not address the hazard: pushvar(symbol randomSeed, 999) followed by an error leaves randomSeed at 999 and the varstack unbalanced, restored only by an explicit popvar. Core.m2:65 already says '-- TODO: move to the interpreter and make thread-safe'. Not filed because no user-visible instance could be constructed: the most promising live site, installPackage.m2:381 pushing printWidth with two deliberate error calls defined just above it, cannot be reached -- forcing one of those errors with a doc node named "Top" fires at document.m2:699 during package load, before the pushvar, and printWidth came back unchanged at 55. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for pushvar, popvar and state-after-interrupt: nothing; #1098 (closed) is about restoring the terminal on SIGSEGV

the effect behind the ask is already delivered, and the residue is cosmetic. setup() (files.m2:488-508) does run unconditionally -- supplantStringFile for ~/.profile-Macaulay2 and ~/.login-Macaulay2, then mungeFile into ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile or ~/.zprofile, with nothing consulting PATH first -- but the snippet it writes is idempotent: bashtempl (files.m2:405-418) prepends a directory only when the variable does not already contain it, and setup-doc.m2 documents exactly that, 'add the appropriate directory to the front of the environment variable PATH ... unless that directory already occurs in the path'. So no duplicate PATH entry results; what the file objects to is only that the init files get edited when there was nothing new to add. Correcting an earlier claim of mine, that nothing checks PATH: nothing in setup() does, but the written snippet does. The maintainer raised the larger question of whether setup() is obsolete. Evidence against: it is referenced from ov_getting_started.m2:231, ov_editors_emacs.m2:92 and distributions/top/INSTALL.in:80 (which runs ./M2 -e 'setup();exit 0'), and users were hitting it recently enough to file #1061, #1138, #1139, #1460 (all closed 2019-2020) and #1068 (open), with real fixes in 480e0899a4 and 4a66fd9023. Evidence for: its audience is now only people installing from the binary tarball into a private location, since packaged installs put M2 on PATH, and the doc's Caveat is about multi-architecture shared home directories, the same dead scenario that settled 1-profile-init. Retiring setup() would mean deciding those three sets of instructions together, which is larger than this row

a question rather than a request -- 'should we do something like this?' over IPython's first-run banner -- and the answer is no, for reasons the pasted banner itself supplies. Its distinctive feature is 'Please press <RETURN> to start IPython', a blocking prompt, which is incompatible with the non-interactive uses that now dominate: M2 --script, capture, example generation and CI. IPython abandoned that banner years ago, so the model is gone too. The underlying behaviour is unchanged: setUpApplicationDirectory (called from packages.m2:331) creates ~/.Macaulay2 with init.m2, code/, local/, an index.html and a README on first run, silently -- observed directly while testing Configuration under a redirected HOME two batches ago, where a fresh home acquired the whole tree and the only output came from the package's own Configuration. The need is served more quietly by that README: a user who looks finds an explanation. A non-blocking one-line notice would be the defensible version, but first-run output is exactly what breaks reproducible example output across the ~8500 .out files, and nobody has asked in seventeen years. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for first-run banners, applicationDirectory and welcome messages: nothing; #2861 is a package update announcement

the mechanism was declined with a reason and the need met another way, both recorded in the source. files.m2:445-450 has the exec-path fix commented out with the explanation beside it: '-- the exec-path fix is not needed, because we exec the shell and ask it to find M2'. What is in emacsfixes instead is ('PATH', currentLayout#"bin", emacsenvtempl), so ~/.emacs-Macaulay2 sets the PATH environment variable, which is what lets emacs's shell find M2 -- the need in the file's one sentence. #67 '.emacs-Maculay2 may also need to set PATH variable' is the tracker's version of the same point and is closed, consistent with PATH now being set. So this is fixed rather than wontfix: the ask names exec-path, the need is that M2 be findable from emacs, and it is

both complaints are gone. The self-shadowing warning in the transcript -- 'symbol fourierMotzkin in FourierMotzkin.Dictionary is shadowed by a symbol in FourierMotzkin.Dictionary', a package shadowing itself, with a fourierMotzkin$0 synonym invented for it -- does not occur. Reproducing it needs a package that is not preloaded, since loadPackage "FourierMotzkin" now refuses with 'package FourierMotzkin not reloaded; try Reload => true'; with Posets and loadPackage(..., LoadDocumentation => true, Reload => true) the only output is ' -- warning: reloading Posets; recreate instances of types from this package', which is the informative warning added by #3852 and credited in this catalog on 1-loadPackage. The second complaint, 'also, the tests didn't run' (check printing nothing in the transcript), is also gone -- check works, as this catalog established on 1-check-inputs where check(0, "Posets") runs 36 tests. #1184 'New notation for shadowed symbols' and #4292 'Stray symbols from packages' are the live open items in this area and neither is this

the ask was granted, and in the shape the file guessed it would be. (sheaf, Ideal) and (sheaf, Variety, Ideal) are both installed -- twelve sheaf methods in all -- and sheaf I for a graded ideal returns a CoherentSheaf. So the file's own reservation was accepted rather than resolved: 'the result should be a sheaf of ideals, not a sheaf of modules; and it seems sort of silly to invent the whole class of sheaves of ideals just so sheaf I will do something. But, why not?' -- no such class was invented, and the result is a sheaf of modules. That is the answer to 'why not', arrived at by doing the cheap half

half done, half unrecoverable. show works: methods.m2:721 declares it, four methods are installed -- Hypertext and URL at html.m2:203,208, TEX at latex.m2:334, RawComputation at engine.m2:408 -- and it is exported, writing a hypertext object out and opening it in a browser, or typesetting and viewing TEX. watch has no definition, no export and no mention anywhere in m2/ or d/, and no commit removed one; a git log -S over 'watch' returns only incidental substring hits in unrelated commits. So there is nothing to recover about what it was meant to do -- a display that updates as a value changes, a debugger watchpoint, both are guesses with nothing to anchor them. A four-word file whose remaining half cannot be reconstructed has no closing condition, and inventing one would be filing an ask Dan did not make. Recorded rather than dropped silently so that anyone who knows what watch meant can revive it. #585 'show the back trace in case of a thrown exception in debug mode' is open and uses the word but is about backtraces
singularLocus(ZZ[x,y]/(11,x)) no longer returns the spurious (11,x,1)
cygwin postinstall and preremove scripts keeping up to 100 backups of site-start.el; those scripts went with M2/distributions/cygwin

a ratio with no target, and the maintainer's question -- gcd of what? -- is the right one, since the file benchmarks only QQ[a,b]. Measured across rings with operands built outside the timing loop: QQ[a,b] gcd 18.7 us against multiply 3.02 us (6.2x), QQ[t] 19.9 vs 3.12 (6.4x), ZZ/32003[a,b] 14.1 vs 2.19 (6.4x), ZZ 3.0 vs 0.37 (8.2x). So the ratio is uniform rather than specific to the case measured, and it has roughly halved since the file was written (11.7 reported, ~6 now) with nobody aiming at it. What the spread does show is that the cost is overhead rather than algorithm: any polynomial gcd is 14-20 us however trivial, gcd of two 200-digit integers is 4.1 us against 3.0 us for gcd(12,18), and real work scales sensibly -- gcd((a+b)^12,(a-b)^12) is 86 us and a pair sharing a degree-12 factor is 230 us. Not filed because there is no stated criterion for success and no profile establishing the overhead is avoidable; the likely answer, conversion to and from Factory, is architectural. One harness correction worth recording: a first pass showed QQ[t] at 36.7 us, apparently slower with one variable than two, because t+1 was being constructed inside the timed loop -- the anomaly was mine. #321 and #1851 are closed; the one open gcd issue, #4583 from this catalog, is about correctness

fixed. The 2007 bug was that smithNormalForm returned its argument unchanged with identity change matrices; Mike's matrix over QQ[x] now gives a genuinely diagonal form, D = diag(1, x-1, x^5-3x^4+x^3+3x^2-x-1), with P*A*Q == D verified true, and the divisibility chain 1 | x-1 | x^5-... is the correct Smith convention. Dan's diagnosis in the reply -- that we need QQ[x, MonomialOrder => Position => Up] 'so that every gb is triangular', and that he should enforce it somehow -- is not what the tree records as the resolution; no fix commit is identified. #3017 'smithNormalForm bug' and #940 'smithNormalForm gives incorrect answer (matrix wrong dimensions)' are both closed and are the tracker's versions of this family; #1580 'smithNormalForm test fails on i386' is still open and is about a different thing. Reproducing this needs matrix{{...}} rather than the file's matrix"..." Classic syntax, which does not accept ^

unchanged after seventeen years, message included: smithNormalForm(matrix{{1}}, ChangeMatrix => {true}) still gives 'array index 1 out of bounds 0 .. 0'. The cause is visible from the call -- ChangeMatrix expects a list of two booleans, one per change matrix, and the caller gave one; {true,false} and {false,true} both work, as the sibling row 1-smithNormalForm2 exercises. So a plausible mistake, since {true} is what someone writes wanting only the first change matrix, produces an internal indexing error naming neither the option nor the expected length. The fix is a length check. Worth filing because it is the last live piece of this family: its two siblings in the same batch both came out fixed, the substantive bugs having been dealt with as #3017 and #940, both closed, leaving only the diagnostic. #1580 'smithNormalForm test fails on i386' is the only open smithNormalForm issue and is an architecture problem. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for ChangeMatrix and the message text: nothing on option validation

the shape bug is gone. The file's complaint is that smithNormalForm(A, ChangeMatrix => {false,true}) returned a 2x2 normal form for a 3x2 input -- 'this normal form doesn't have the right shape!' -- while the other two option settings returned 3x2. Today all three agree: for A = matrix{{-1,1},{1,1},{1,1}} the normal form is matrix{{1,0},{0,2},{0,0}} whether ChangeMatrix is omitted, {true,false} or {false,true}. The divisibility order also improved: the file shows {{2,0},{0,1},{0,0}} and it is now 1 then 2, which is the correct Smith convention. The file's own guess, 'it must be related to the KeepZeroes option', is not corroborated -- no fix commit identified. #3017 and #940, both closed, are the tracker's versions

two of three clauses unmet, and the measurements are worse than the file's. Interruptability is met: alarm 2 during a 45-second sort interrupts it. The speed clause is not: sorting 50000 equal elements takes 19.96 s against the file's target of .01 s, and pre-sorted distinct input is worse still at 45.73 s, where the same 50000 values shuffled sort in .061 s -- a factor of 750. Quadratic, established by scaling rather than one point: pre-sorted 10000 takes 1.79 s, 20000 takes 7.22 s (4.0x for 2x the data) and 40000 takes 35.7 s (4.9x). Duplication scales the same way: random from 0..99 is .447 s, all-equal is 19.96 s. internalsort is a recursive quicksort at actors3.d:477-509 (sortfun -> basicsort2, setupfun at :535); the pivot is already randomized, 'a := randomint() % b' at :479, which is why random input is fast and why the pre-sorted collapse is surprising -- the naive diagnosis is wrong. A per-call linear shift runs after both recursive calls, 'for k from l+1 to j do sortlist.(k-1) = sortlist.k', which is worth examining, but I did not establish it as the cause and the issue says so. The third clause, tallying duplicates first, would address the 19.96 s case and not the 45.73 s one. List construction was excluded from the timings (toList(0..49999) is .008 s). Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues: #101 and #650 are open and about sort's semantics, not its speed; nothing on complexity

sort accepts a function: sort({3,1,2}, x -> -x) returns {3,2,1}. The tracker's version, #1154 'feature request: sort accept order function', is closed. Worth recording the semantics, since the file asks for a 'comparison function' and what exists is a key function -- the second argument is applied to each element and the results compared, which is why x -> -x sorts descending rather than being read as a two-argument comparator. That covers the common case and composes with inversePermutation and the rest, and a genuine comparator would be a different signature. #4529, 'sort(List) advertises DegreeOrder and MonomialOrder, which it ignores', is closed and was filed from this catalog

unmet -- options sort is {DegreeOrder => null, MonomialOrder => Ascending}, with no Permutation -- but the capability is one composition away and nobody has asked in seventeen years. sort(toList(0..#L-1), i -> L#i) returns the permutation, using the key-function form that this same batch recorded as fixed on 1-sort-function; inversePermutation exists as a MethodFunction, so the file's cross-reference target is there, just unreferenced from sort. sortColumns is the precedent for returning an ordering rather than the sorted object, for matrices, which is where the need actually arose. Two notes for anyone revisiting: the one-liner is not discoverable, which is the real gap and would be a documentation fix rather than an option; and a Permutation option would run through the same internalsort that 1-sort is filed against in this batch, so it would inherit the quadratic behaviour on ordered input. the ask names fillMatrix and the constant case, and that is what was done. genmat.m2:118-148 now has three paths: all degrees zero goes to randommat, a single rawRandomConstantMatrix call; one non-zero degree goes to basis(deg,R) * randommat, still one bulk fill; only mixed degrees fall through to randomElement := memoize(deg -> ...), which builds entries individually. a tentative suggestion -- 'Maybe we should turn on this option in the debug mode' -- superseded from both ends. configure.ac carries no -fstack-protector, no _FORTIFY_SOURCE and no hardening flags at all, so it is literally unmet. But release builds get hardened by whoever packages M2: Debian and Ubuntu apply -fstack-protector-strong and -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 through dpkg-buildflags and Fedora through its macros, and GCC on those distributions defaults to -fstack-protector-strong anyway -- which matters more since M2 stopped shipping its own packaging (beeb464469, 6c833cbf0c), so the builds users install are not M2's. And the debug case the file actually names is better served by the sanitizer builds the tree supports: AddressSanitizer catches the same buf[101]=12 and reports the offending write with a location, where -fstack-protector only notices a smashed canary at function return and aborts. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for stack-protector, hardening, _FORTIFY_SOURCE and fsanitize: nothing; #573 and #1431 are compiler-compatibility problems

unmet and not worth the cost. Triple quotes are not a delimiter: zzs = """abc""" gives 'no method for adjacent objects: "abc" (of class String) SPACE "" (of class String)', so it parses as three juxtaposed strings, an empty one either side of a normal one, and /// remains the only verbatim form. The file proposes replacing /// rather than adding an alternative, and /// is load-bearing across Macaulay2Doc and every package that writes documentation, including the doc ///...///  idiom itself, so a replacement is a breaking change across the ecosystem for a syntax preference borrowed from Python. Adding """ alongside would not be free either: "" is a valid empty string and adjacent juxtaposition already gives """" a meaning, so the grammar interaction needs resolving rather than just admitting the token. Nothing in seventeen years has asked. a request for a computer-algebra layer M2 does not have, recorded as one user's wish in two lines with no defect and no specification. What exists is an Expression hierarchy -- Sum, Product, Power, Divide, BinaryOperation, Holder, with hold to build one and expressionValue to evaluate it -- but it exists to render mathematics, being what net, describe and texMath are built on, not to manipulate it: expand is an unbound symbol, expressionValue is Core-private, and nothing simplifies, collects terms or substitutes into an unevaluated expression. M2's answer to symbolic expansion and substitution is to work in an actual ring, where QQ[x,y] gives both with real semantics; the cases that do not fit a ring are exactly the ones a CAS handles and M2 does not. 'Expansion, substitution, etc.' is a project without a boundary, so an issue would have no closing condition. Searched cache, PRs and gh search issues for symbolic algebra, computer algebra, expand and symbolic manipulation: nothing. The adjacent items are #1754, 'Wishlist: Make Expressions work with inequalities', and #4595, filed from this catalog today for not Expression -- both adding operators to Expression, a long way short of a manipulation layer

three words with no reason -- 'eliminate ultimate!' -- against a function that is still central. class ultimate is MethodFunction, it is exported (exports.m2:1252), documented by reference from coefficientRing-doc.m2:29,31 with a SeeAlso, and used at seven Core call sites for walking ring towers: basis.m2:288 (with its own '-- is ambient better or coefficientRing?'), complexes.m2:14, galois.m2:47, gb.m2:118, mutablemat.m2:237, newring.m2:239, quotring.m2:286. Removing it is a refactor of tower walking throughout Core justified by nothing the file states. One thing worth recording in case that was the objection: the definition at methods.m2:526-529 is a try-wrapped fixed-point loop, 'while try (ox := x; x = f x; ox =!= x) else false do ()', so any error from f silently ends the iteration and returns whatever was reached -- the same error-masking shape as the old liftable, which this catalog recorded as fixed when #2726 removed its try. That would be a smaller and separable change than eliminating the function, if anyone wants it

the same question as bugs/dan/1-setting-state, settled wontfix in this same session, asked about one variable rather than in general: 'path = prepend(tmp,path); -- how to undo this if the next line has an error?'. The answer has not changed. pushvar/popvar (Core.m2:67-73) is the mechanism that exists, and it does not restore on error -- pushing a value and then raising leaves the value changed and the varstack unbalanced -- so M2 has no unwind-protect and the comment's question still has no good answer. path is not among the eight globals Core guards with pushvar, so nothing has been done for this case specifically either. Settled the same way as its general form for consistency; Core.m2:65 already carries '-- TODO: move to the interpreter and make thread-safe', which is where a real fix would start

the need is met, and one level up from where the file proposed it. separateExampleOutput does not exist -- it is a bare Symbol -- but separateM2output does (examples.m2:22-25), splitting on M2outputRE = "\n+(?=i+[1-9][0-9]* : )", which is exactly 'separate input/output pairs', and makeExampleItem PRE at :40 applies it automatically: 'PRE \ M2CODE \ separateM2output s' for every PRE inside an EXAMPLE. So the user writes EXAMPLE { PRE ///.../// }, which is the file's own syntax minus the separator call, and gets the pairs without invoking anything -- the proposed function is unnecessary rather than missing. In live use: BeginningMacaulay2/tutorial:10 and elsewhere with EXAMPLE { PRE ///M2/// }, and the SCSCP documentation with EXAMPLE { PRE get (...) } for whole captured transcripts. No fix commit identified

the need is met, by a different mechanism than the one proposed -- and the file is explicit that the mechanism was not the point, ending 'somehow'. .github/workflows/build-dmg.yml builds M2 on both Apple Silicon and Intel runners, its header reading 'It runs on both Intel (x86_64) and Apple Silicon (arm64) runners' with arch: arm64 and arch: x86_64 matrix entries, so a Mac user of either architecture gets a working M2. Nothing in the tracker or in comments about universal binaries or lipo

unmet, no symptom, and the proposed replacement is itself superseded. scclib.c:512 still calls utime(cname,&buf) and types.h:92 still includes <utime.h>. The premise has strengthened rather than expired -- POSIX.1-2008 removed utime() outright, where the macOS man page the file quotes only called it obsoleted -- but glibc and the BSDs still provide it as a compatibility interface, so nothing breaks and nothing is scheduled to. And the successor the file names, utimes, has since been superseded in turn by utimensat, so implementing the note as written would swap one obsolete interface for another. The gain from utimensat, nanosecond timestamps, buys M2 nothing here since setFileTime is used for install timestamps. Nothing in the tracker or in comments mentions utime, utimes or setFileTime

there is a validation target, and a better validator than the one the file names. packages/Makefile.in:132 defines validate-html, which runs html5validator --show-warnings over @pre_prefix@/@tail_htmldir@/$PACKAGE/html for every package in ALL_PACKAGES, accumulating the failures into INVALID_PACKAGES and reporting them; the comment above it records the dependency, 'requires html5validator: python3 -m pip install html5validator'. So 'use validate program to validate all our html!' is done, against the WHATWG validator rather than the older W3C validate. It is a standalone target rather than part of check, which matches how the sibling Info-validate target was handled -- commented out at :121-122 with 'the Info-validate function doesn't work well enough to be useful', a decision this catalog recorded when settling the info-menu row. #706 'generating valid html' and #2757 are closed

unmet, and filed on the embedding argument at the maintainer's suggestion rather than on the file's own framing. methods value has eight entries -- String, Nothing, IndexedVariableTable, IndexedVariable, RingElement, Pseudocode, Expression, Symbol -- and none takes a dictionary or list of them, so value resolves against the ambient dictionaryPath with no per-call override. The only workaround is assigning the global around the call, which is the hazard bugs/dan/1-setting-state describes and which pushvar/popvar does not fix. The maintainer asked whether this would be useful for a possible future Macaulay2 C API, and the argument is stronger there than at M2 level: a host cannot unwind an assignment if value raises, having no try across the boundary; several evaluation contexts in one process cannot share one global path, which is Macaulay2Web's shape; and a host needs to say where new symbols from 'x = 3' land. There is no top-level embedding API in the tree today -- e/interface/ is the engine's C interface, a different layer -- so the issue is framed as the primitive such an API would need, noting that localDictionaries and its use at code.m2:20 already express 'these dictionaries for this scope'. Checked as a sibling when 1-Package-dictionary was settled and confirmed not the same ask, that row being about dictionaryPath ordering. #917, #1427 and #1627 are dictionary-hygiene issues, none this

an option requested 'in some future version' with no motivating problem, and nothing has asked in seventeen years. Unmet: degreesRing R still uses T unconditionally and there is no monoid option to name it. The lines the file quotes moved from ofcm.m2 to monoids.m2:587 but are otherwise the same, including the aside Dan flagged -- 'M.degreesRing = if opts.Heft =!= null then degreesRing heftvec else degreesRing degrk; -* shouldn't really be needed *-' -- so the code is intact and only its address changed, which is why this is not obsolete. same subject as #2025 'Creating ring variables from strings', open since 2021. Its own symptom has changed: it reports QQ["x_1"] failing with 'baseName: no base name available' on the first try and succeeding on the second, and today it fails consistently on both, with the clearer message -- so the erratic half is fixed and what remains is that the capability is absent. the information is in the version table, in the git equivalents of what the file asks for. the fatal half is gone and the residue is a wording question nobody has raised. In 2008 viewHelp (symbol^, RR, QQ) aborted with 'documentation key for RR ^ QQ encountered, but no method installed'; today help (symbol^, RR, QQ) prints the same complaint as a diagnostic and returns a document anyway -- DIV{HEADER1{RR ^ QQ}, DIV{COMMENT{empty documentation body}}, ...} -- so the call succeeds. The complaint is still technically wrong for the reason Dan demonstrates with lookup and code: lookup(symbol^, RR, Ring) resolves, to lift, since RingElement ^ Ring := Number ^ Ring := (x,R) -> lift(x,R) covers it by inheritance, and the key check tests exact installation rather than lookup. But the document it produces is empty, so the message is right about the substance -- nothing is documented for that key -- and what is left is that it is labelled 'error' for a case that returns a value. The file records an observation without asking for anything, and nothing has been reported since. #987, #1006, #1516 and #975 are the closed viewHelp issues, none of them this

the concern is addressed, and by the mechanism the file implies. It asks 'What if the documentation is found in the applicationDirectory and not in the prefixDirectory? Then viewHelp won't find it', quoting a viewHelp that hardcodes prefixDirectory | htmlFilename key. distribute M2 for Windows as a VMware virtual appliance, the way Sage did in 2008. Sage stopped, the linked modular.math.washington.edu path is long gone, and M2's Windows story is not this

five words naming two products, one of which is dead. 'try VirtualBox and AndLinux' -- AndLinux, which ran Linux inside Windows via coLinux, has had no release since about 2011 and its approach was superseded by WSL, for which M2 has its own wiki page, Installing-Macaulay2-in-WSL. four asks under one speculative mechanism -- 'gc seems to offer support now for weak pointers ... we could use them for' -- none of which uses weak pointers today; there is no GC_register_disappearing_link or equivalent anywhere in d/ or e/. Measured, one by one. (4) 'making R^1 always give the same answer' is met: R^1 === R^1 is true, by ordinary memoization rather than by weak pointers. (3) is not: M === N is true for two constructions of R^2 while symmetricAlgebra M === symmetricAlgebra N is false, exactly the failure the file names, 'currently symmetricAlgebra doesn't have it' -- but that follows from results being cached in each object's own cacheTable rather than in a global table keyed on (F,A), so the honest fix is the redesign the file asks for, ending 'Eliminate cacheTables!'. (2) is not: QQ[u,v] === QQ[u,v] is false for two separate constructions, where the file notes 'Sage returns the same ring every time!'. (1) is partial: openFiles exists as a registry. So what remains is a caching redesign rather than a defect, and an issue for it would have no closing condition. #486 is the open pointer-related issue and is about engine error returns

a 2008 punch list against a web site that no longer exists in that form: the documentation on the site should be updated to 0.9.95, the 'some chapters online' section of the book could go, some 'Other downloads' entries are not current, and several 'Related links' are dead. a research task with its reading list attached, and its status already recorded where M2 records such things. The file is 'fix test/testmulti.m2' plus three references -- Eisenbud, Mustata and Stillman on cohomology of toric varieties and local cohomology with monomial supports; Cox on the homogeneous coordinate ring of a toric variety; Batyrev and Cox on Hodge structure of projective hypersurfaces in toric varieties. The test survives as tests/quarantine/testmulti.m2, headed 'Test of multi-homogeneity. This should include: hilbert functions, gb's, syzygies, resolutions, basis, homogeneity (?), ...' over rings such as ZZ/101[a..d, Degrees=>{{1,-1},{1,0},{2,-2},{3,4}}]. quarantine is this catalog's own vocabulary for a known-failing reproducer not worth blocking CI over, so the test's state is formally on record and an issue would restate it, with no specific failing assertion to close against. Its sibling 1-weighted-proj.m2 is adjacent but distinct, being about singularLocus of a weighted Proj

settled on the one testable claim in a 203-line mail thread. Dan writes 'We also compute the singularLocus of a weighted projective space incorrectly', with A = ZZ/101[x,y,z,Degrees=>{1,1,2}] and X = Proj A. That is no longer true: singularLocus X now errors with 'expected variables all of the same degree' rather than returning a wrong answer, so M2 refuses instead of lying -- the better of the two failure modes, though not the same as working. Recording this as fixed should not be read as weighted projective spaces working: the file's opening line, 'Sheaf cohomology and the cotangent sheaf have to have algorithms developed for computing them', is untouched, and that is a research programme rather than a defect -- an issue for it would have no closing condition. The rest of the file is correspondence with Yang-Hui He about Proj of weighted rings, with references to Eisenbud-Mustata-Stillman, Cox, and Batyrev-Cox. No fix commit identified

the same defect this catalog filed as #4531, 'Documentation html filenames still contain raw UTF-8', which is open. verbatim the same ask as 1-CC-tostring, settled in an earlier batch: the two files differ only in wording, this one closing 'Or should it?' where the other says 'Do it for matrices before 1.1'. 530ef987f8 (2008-02-03, 'print complex numbers to a combined precision for both parts') carried both parts to a common accuracy, which is what 'go the same distance to the right of the point in the two parts' asks for. decided by the file's own author, twice, and the losing option is still in the source as a comment. a1acd9565f (2008-10-27) is titled in part 'add class Holder2, which holds both a print form and a value form, make expression use Holder2 appropriately for monoid elements and ring elements' -- Dan implemented this file's proposal by name. ff94baa8f2 (2008-11-01, five days later) is 'put "value hold symbol x" back the way it was; comment out Holder2', and Holder2 survives only as commented-out lines at expressions.m2:128-130,140-145,153. The trade-off he took instead is stated above them at :114-116: 'with the following line we have no way to distinguish between "hold symbol x" and "hold x" when x has a value: but without it, we have no way to recover a polynomial from its expression, without introducing Holder2 or something like it', over expressionValue Symbol := value. Measured today in the file's own order: case 1 (value hold x === x) false, case 2 (value expression y === y) true, case 3 (value expression M_0 === M_0, M a bare monoid) false, case 4 (value expression S_0 === S_0) true -- so the 2008 revert traded case 1 for cases 2 and 4, and case 3 fails only because a bare monoid never binds the global z so there is no value to recover. Nothing documents value expression x === x as a promise; ov_language.m2:7 is the only mention of hold. Searched issues and PRs for Holder, hold expression, expression value: #1754 and #4595 are Expression arithmetic, #4510 is symbol reuse, none is this

the ask names no routine and the capability behind it is reached already. Direct NTL use in the engine is lattice reduction only -- the sole includes under Macaulay2/e/ are NTL/LLL.h, NTL/mat_ZZ.h and NTL/ZZ.h, and the only NTL:: symbols are mat_ZZ, ZZ, SetSeed, ZZFromBytes, BytesFromZZ, NumBytes -- surfacing as rawLLL (interface.dd:4117) and LLL(m, Strategy => NTL) in LLLBases. But NTL's factorization and gcd routines are reached through factory: libraries/factory/Makefile.in:31,49 configures it --with-ntl and then greps _config.h for 'HAVE_NTL 1', failing the build without it, and configure.ac:600 records the dependency as deliberate. Where M2 has wanted more since 2006 it went elsewhere -- fplll as a second LLL backend (e/fplll-interface.cpp), FLINT for bignum, finite fields and polynomial arithmetic, givaro/fflas-ffpack/linbox for exact linear algebra, MPFR/MPFI for precision. Searched the tracker for NTL: 33 hits, every one a build or version-compatibility issue (#147, #214, #467, #2153, #2244). Nobody has asked for a routine in twenty years. The one file that does name one, 5-NTL-LLL (hermite), keeps its own row

The same commit added test/smith.m2. Verified: smithNormalForm matrix{{2,4,4},{-6,6,12},{10,4,16}} returns diag(2,2,156) with the divisibility chain, P*A*Q == D, and over QQ[x] a rank-1 example diagonalizes correctly. the need is met in every case the file names; the uniform API it sketches was never built. Its central ask -- 'I should always give a map from C or from C_0 to M, when C = res M, because it is not always the case that coker C.dd_1 and M will be equal' -- is answered by augmentationMap (Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:1151-1154, added with the package in 2f5b7b03d4, 2019-05-24), and res is freeResolution from Complexes now, so it is reachable from res M directly. Verified the premise still holds and the map exists: for M = subquotient(matrix{{a,b}}, matrix{{a*c}}) over QQ[a,b,c], coker C.dd_1 == M is false while augmentationMap C returns a ComplexMap whose target complex has M in degree 0. prune gives M.cache.pruningMap and it inverts with ^-1; trim needs no map, trim M == M. three of the four asks are met and the fourth is #2267. (1) 'make package/Makefile run check P for each package P': packages/Makefile.in:49-57 generates a check-$(pkg) target per package running check(pkg, UserMode=>false, Verbose=>...) and hangs them all off check::. the operator has been right associative since six years before the file, and the question is really which of two constituencies to serve. binding.d:276 reads 'export ColonS := makeKeyword(binaryright(":"));', introduced by aabb502945 (2000-06-11) and never changed -- checked the file as of 2006 and it is identical. getParsing on : returns {40,39,-1}, and 40 == 39+1 is the very predicate the manual uses to generate its list of right-associative operators (ov_language.m2:1181-1183), so : is published as right associative. The file's own transcript proves it: 3 : 2 : x giving ((x,x),(x,x),(x,x)) is only reachable under right grouping. What the other transcript shows is the tension -- verified over QQ[a,b,c] with I = ideal(a*b,a*c), P1 = ideal a, P2 = ideal(b,c): I : P1 : P2 is ideal(c,b) (i.e. I : (P1 : P2)) while (I : P1) : P2 is ideal 1, which is why Dan parenthesized. Repetition wants right, iterated ideal quotient wants left, and changing it now would silently re-group every n : x in the tree. Searched the tracker for associative/right associative: #1238 and #2609 are both about ^, nothing about :

six of the eight options are in libraries/gc/Makefile.in today, adopted one at a time: --enable-threads=posix by efb1b2e9e8 (2008-01-07, 'compile gc with pthreads support'), --enable-parallel-mark by a15c2efeda (2008-09-24, 'update gc configuration options for parallel marking'), --enable-cplusplus by 25e097a46e (2012-01-26), --enable-static and --enable-shared conditionally at :60-62, and LARGE_CONFIG's effect written out explicitly as -DMAX_HEAP_SECTS=81920 -DMAXHINCR=4096 by 122b8e3e3e (2022-04-17, 'arrange always to build libgc for large memory configurations'), which is what that macro sets. ALL_INTERIOR_POINTERS and --enable-thread-local-alloc are bdwgc defaults from 7.x onward and we are on 8.2.12, so neither needs stating. Only --enable-redirect-malloc was never adopted, and it is the one with real risk. Note this Makefile applies only when gc is built from source; a distribution build links the system libgc
a 2006 user report of building M2 under Cygwin against a SAGE spkg, needing CPPFLAGS=-D_setmode=setmode. The cygwin distribution was removed in 2021 (51d82cd738)

all three parts of the email are documented, and the last of them arrived in 2022. The behavior and its rationale -- 'the making of the ring may involve setting that variable so its value is the corresponding indeterminate ... that's by design' -- is the Consequences of (use,Ring) at use-doc.m2:36-77: 'All variables of R are set to global variables. Additionally, certain operations creating elements of R are installed globally', followed by 'When a ring (or a monoid) is assigned to a global variable, this function is automatically called for it', and a Caveat that values previously stored in those variables are lost. the order Watt proposed is not what M2 does, and what M2 does is deliberate, documented and load-bearing. lookupBinaryMethod at hashtables.dd:536-556 is a plain nested loop -- outer over ancestors of the left class, inner over ancestors of the right -- so the entire right chain is exhausted before the left advances one step, which is lexicographic rather than Watt's homogeneous order by total depth. The 'inheritance' node at ov_methods.m2:208-231 picks exactly the case where the two schemes disagree, installs Y + X and X + Z with Y and Z both children of X, states the result, and explains the mechanism: 'after enough unsuccessful iterations of this, the second type is reset to Z, the first type is replaced by its parent, and the search continues', adding that the same order applies to method functions. Reproduced it: y + z gives 'Y + X', where Watt's order has the two candidates tied at total depth 1. Changing it would silently reselect methods anywhere both a left-more-specific and a right-more-specific candidate exist, with no error, in every package. The file claims no defect and ends on 'Is there an efficient way to do it?', which was never answered; nothing on the tracker, #895 and #1076 are closed and about module structure. This is a judgment, stated so a maintainer can overrule it cheaply

unmet, deliberately, and the file prices the change itself. One line does it: EngineRing / Ideal at quotring.m2:179 reads 'gensgbI := generators gb gensI', so the Groebner basis is computed when the quotient ring is constructed, and nothing in quotring.m2 or gb.m2 defers anything. Measured rather than asserted, with the operands built outside the timing: over ZZ/32003[a..e] with a five-generator ideal, gb I on its own costs 0.245s and making R/I costs 0.265s, so essentially the whole cost of the quotient ring is the basis, paid whether or not anything is ever reduced in it. A first probe missed this and is worth recording -- the basis is cached on the generator matrix, not on the ideal, so I.cache shows only QuotientRing afterwards and looks innocent. Against doing it: normal form, equality and hashing in a quotient ring all rest on that basis, so computing it at construction is what makes a QuotientRing a defined object rather than a promise, and the file names both consequences of deferring it -- unreduced elements visible at top level, and 'the hash code of a ring element needs to be computed from the normal form'. Searched lazy, lazily, lazy Groebner, normal form quotient ring on the tracker and in the cache: nothing. This is a judgment, stated so it can be overruled cheaply

reproduces, and is worse than the three-line file claims. In 2006 localDictionaries global a returned {Macaulay2#"private dictionary"}; today it returns {Varieties#"private dictionary"}, and the same answer comes back for global sin, for symbol currentPackage, and for a symbol nobody has ever defined -- so it carries no information about its argument at all, and the name drifting between the two runs is the tell that it is whichever package was created last. Three things are wrong with it. It is not local: class of the result is GlobalDictionary, where the documented example localDictionaries ((f 22) 33) correctly gives three LocalDictionary and localDictionaries() gives one. And it does not contain the symbol: #?"a" and #?"sin" are both false on the returned dictionary. The documentation at ov_repl.m2:462-479 promises 'a list of the local dictionaries associated with the lexical scopes containing f', and a global symbol has no enclosing local scope, so {} or an error is the defensible answer. Searched localDictionaries, local dictionary, dictionary global symbol on the tracker and scanned the cache: the only hit is #4605, which this catalog filed from 1-value-dictionary-path and is about value and dictionary resolution

unmet, and declined rather than merely undone. The file is word for word the twin of 2-p-adic-numbers three rows away -- same 'new low level class', same 'this should parallel real numbers, so we don't create the ring unless it's asked for' -- and that twin came out fixed in this same batch, by the Padic package, whose PadicFieldFamily is the only 'new Type of RingFamily' in the tree outside Core's own InexactFieldFamily. There is no counterpart for integers mod n: ZZ/n still builds a QuotientRing, and ZZ/5 =!= ZZ/5. The asks are not as parallel as the wording suggests, which is the reason for the verdict: Q_p had no representation in M2 at all, whereas ZZ/n already exists, is cheap to construct, and is the spelling every package and every user writes, so a second low-level representation would need promotion, lifting and equality against the existing one and would buy a construction cost that is not the bottleneck. Searched ZZ/n class, integers mod n, low level class and RingFamily on the tracker and scanned the cache: nothing proposes it. A judgment, and the Padic template means it would be cheap to revisit

'make this work: (a,,b) = (1,2,3)' -- it works, assigning 1 to a and 3 to b and discarding the middle value, where the file's transcript shows a syntax error. Deliberate rather than incidental: evaluate.d:1285 handles the empty slot explicitly with 'is nullCode do values.i', added by 5465eb92e1 (2025-04-20, 'Add support for parallel assignment of other operators') and shipped in PR #3748, 'Improvements to parallel assignment', merged 2026-03-17, whose description has a section headed 'Partial parallel assignment' carrying this exact example. It is tested: tests/normal/parallel.m2:93-97, under a '-- null' heading, asserts (a, , , b) = (9, 10, 11, 12) with two empty slots and a ??= variant. I first recorded it as untested because I grepped for ',,' and the file writes ', ,' with a space -- a narrowing grep read as an honest negative. Documentation: the syntax is covered by the language-wide rule at ov_lists.m2:159-166, 'Omitting an element of a list causes the symbol null to be inserted in its place', with the example A = {3,4,,5}. What I could not find in any node is the assignment semantics of such a null on the left -- that the corresponding value is discarded rather than erroring; the 'multiple assignment' and 'multiple local assignment' nodes (operators/assignment.m2:156, :477) say only that the number of expressions must match the number of variables, and neither doc commit in the PR, 1a7fa3e09a or 54df9825c1, adds it. asked for 'a new low level class for p-adic numbers to a certain precision' that 'should parallel real numbers, so we don't create the ring unless it's asked for', and that is the Padic package, added by 67e24f06e9 (2026-04-21) and written by the maintainer of this branch. The parallel is exact rather than approximate: PadicFieldFamily is 'new Type of RingFamily' at Padic.m2:213, which is the same parent InexactFieldFamily has, so QQ_7 stands to RR as the note asked. Verified: class QQ_7 is PadicFieldFamily and parent of it is RingFamily, exactly as for RR and InexactFieldFamily; QQ_7(12/7) prints 5*7^-1 + 1 with 'of precision 20' in the type line, mirroring RR's 'of precision 53'; an explicit precision is a first argument, QQ_7(30, 3) reporting precision 30; and addition and multiplication work across precisions. Implemented over FLINT through the ForeignFunctions interface, and written up in arXiv 2604.16799. Eighteen years between the note and the package. Its twin 2-mod-n-class, asking the same thing for integers mod n in the same words, is the row that did not land

two of the three numbered tasks are met and the third reproduces with a sharper example than the file's. (1) 'make res keep going past the gdim of the ring if necessary': over ZZ[], global dimension 1, the resolution has length 2. (3) 'work on making res over ZZ[x1,...,xn] stop at the gdim': over ZZ[x,y] it has length 3, which is the gdim. (2) 'find out why res plugged in the presentation matrix as dd_1 in the first example and make it do better': running the file's own example, ZZ[] and random(R^6,R^9), freeResolution gives ranks {6,9,3} with dd_1 equal to the presentation matrix -- and the Smith normal form of that matrix is six units, so the module is zero, which minimalPresentation confirms with a 0x0 presentation. A length-2 free resolution of the zero module. The cause is a top-of-the-tower guard: resolutionOverZZ at Complexes/FreeResolution.m2:417-419 opens 'if R =!= ZZ then return null', and it is the hook that prunes, since it calls minimalPresentation; ZZ[] is not ZZ, so Strategy => 1 answers instead, confirmed by reading M.cache.ResolutionObject.Strategy, which is null over ZZ and 1 over ZZ[]. I first wrote this up as a ZZ defect and that was wrong: coker id^3 gives {0} over ZZ but {3,3} over ZZ[], ZZ[x] and QQ[x] alike, so ZZ is the exception rather than the rule, and minimalBetti inherits the non-minimal answer where minimize does not. FreeResolution.m2:573-576 already cites #3785 next to a commented-out LLL hook carrying the same 'ring M === ZZ' guard; #3785's own example passes now because res is freeResolution

three sentences, and the only one naming a defect is fixed. the first ask is met and the rest is #1026. 'fix this to output (,,) instead' -- toExternalString (,,) returns (,,) now, not (null,null,null), and value of it gives back the same three-element sequence. Of the ring block, frac A, ambient B, B^3 and C^4 all round-trip through value; two do not, and the file's order gives a sharper reproducer than the file itself has. Minimal: A = ZZ[a,b]; B = A/(a^2-1); value toExternalString B fails with 'expected element of the same ring or promotable to it', because the emitted string is A/(a^2-1) and by then the global a is bound to an element of B rather than of A -- 'use A' first and the identical string evaluates fine. frac C fails the same way through the x..y range form, x having become a ring element. The last complaint, that map(oo^1,,{{x}}) printing map(QQ [x]^{{0}}, QQ [x]^{{-1}}, {{x}}) 'is worthless', is fixed where the ring has a name: W = QQ[w] gives map(W^1,W^{{-1}},{{w}}) and that round-trips; with oo there is no name to emit. #1026 is exactly this, its own example being the file's last one, and its diagnosis -- 'one needs to have the ring and its generators as global variables' -- is the whole of it, the quotient case being the generators half. Settled as (b): a comment on #1026 adds the named-ring reproducer, since #1026's example needs an anonymous ring and this one does not. Note the autorun 'fail' is meaningless here -- the file opens with a line of prose, so it was never a runnable script

one line, 'add Version option to uninstallPackage', resting on a premise M2 has never had. There are no side-by-side versioned installs: the layout is share/doc/Macaulay2/PKG/ with no version component, uninstallPackage takes exactly one option today, InstallPrefix (installPackage.m2:887), and installPackage's nineteen options (:640-662) include nothing version-related either. Its body removes every file matching the package name across both layouts, so only one version of a package exists under a prefix at a time and a Version option would have nothing to select between. Granting the ask means versioning the install layout first, which is a far larger change than the line proposes and which nobody has asked for in twenty years. There is a coherent smaller reading -- Version as a guard, refusing to uninstall unless the installed version matches -- but the file does not say that, and filing it would be substituting my idea for Dan's. The related #797, 'uninstallPackage doesn't remove everything', is closed. A judgment, stated so it can be overruled cheaply

a hand-maintained inventory, superseded by machinery that keeps itself current. two asks, both answered, and the first is a duplicate of a row settled earlier in this catalog. 'res, trim and prune return new modules ... but they don't return the maps, instead they cache them somewhere, which isn't very intuitive' is the same complaint as 2-cached-maps, which came out fixed: augmentationMap gives the map from a resolution to the module (Complexes/ChainComplex.m2:1151-1154), prune records pruningMap and it inverts, and trim needs no map since trim M == M. The second half, 'if we do T = tensor(R,S) then the user needs a reliable way to get the ring maps from R and S into T ... how can anyone reasonably use the result of graphIdeal', is answered by the two-argument map: verified over QQ[a] and QQ[b] that map(T, R) gives map(T,zzR,{a}) and map(T, S) gives map(T,zzS,{b}). That is not something tensor returns -- T.cache holds only 'module' -- but it is a documented way to get them, and graphIdeal RingMap exists at newring.m2:97. a working code sketch rather than a defect report -- a recursive merge over nested OptionTables, with the note that 'this code could be installed in functions like gb that have lots of optional arguments to provide a hierarchy of optional arguments'. both halves of the thread, and both verified numerically rather than by inspection. Mike's question, whether to allow the rational reconstruction algorithm between QQ and ZZ/p, is answered: liftZZmodQQ at quotring.m2:64 is installed as lift(S,QQ) at :108, and lift(37_(ZZ/101), QQ) returns 10/3, which checks out -- 3 inverse mod 101 is 34, so 10*34 = 340 = 37 + 3*101. The engine carries the machinery under its own name, cra.hpp and interface/cra.h being headed 'Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction'. Dan's addendum, 'lifting QQ --> RRR or RR can be done with continued fractions, we should do that too', is met by lift(RR,QQ) at reals.m2:228 via rawToRational: lift(0.1,QQ) is 1/10 and lift(1/3.0,QQ) is 1/3, neither of which is the exact binary value, and lift(sqrt 2, QQ) is 209064253/147830751 -- a convergent, where the exact value would have denominator near 2^52. No fix commit recorded: both arrived piecewise and I could not tie either to one change

declined by its author in the message that proposes it. Dan writes 'I think two tallies should be weakly equal only if their elements and multiplicities are weakly equal ... Maybe I'll implement that. It'll be way slow, so maybe I won't. Meanwhile, I'm removing the method.' The example still fails exactly as written: over QQ[x,y,z], set {ideal(x,y), ideal(x,y,z)} == set {ideal(y,x), ideal(y,z,x)} is false while ideal(x,y) == ideal(y,x) is true, and tally behaves the same way, though set {1,2} == set {2,1} is true -- so container equality goes through hashing and ===, not ==. The second email sketches the way to make it affordable, a per-class tuple of 'discriminators' such as ring, poincare and gens @@ gb with a flag for whether the set is complete; none of that exists. Hash-based containers need === to find an element at all, so changing this means either quadratic membership or building the discriminator machinery, which is research-sized. Searched the tracker for tally and set equality: #690 is closed and unrelated, nothing tracks this

a 2005 transcript from Macaulay 2 version 0.9.20 on a 2.4.22 kernel, where getWWW answered 'can't open socket : Servname not supported for ai_socktype'. getWWW "https://macaulay2.com/" returns 16569 bytes today. Dan's documentation-writing tutorial to Amelia Taylor, and the advice in it ended up on the wiki rather than in the tree -- checked there first, per the rule that a documentation request may be answered somewhere git grep cannot see. the file asks whether the wrapping is nice -- 'This is not such a nice way to wrap things' over a version hash table broken by a horizontal rule with the closing brace stranded and the tail after a blank line -- and the same question was asked and answered on the tracker as #1380, 'printWidth not obeyed consistently', closed 2020-07-08. the file asks someone to find out whether NTL has a hermite routine, so here is the answer: it has one, and it cannot be offered as another strategy without restricting the input. NTL/HNF.h declares exactly one function, 'void HNF(mat_ZZ& W, const mat_ZZ& A, const ZZ& D)', where D is the determinant of the full-rank lattice generated by the rows of A -- so it needs a square full-rank matrix and its determinant known in advance, where hermite (LLLBases.m2:634-651) accepts any matrix over ZZ and errors on anything but Strategy => LLL. HNF matches nothing under Macaulay2/e/, so it is not linked. The sibling 2-NTL came out wontfix in this same session on the wider ground that NTL's role has narrowed -- the engine uses it for lattice reduction only, factorization reaches it through factory, and what M2 acquired since went to fplll, FLINT and givaro. A judgment, and the signature is recorded here so nobody has to look it up again

a recipe from Wolfram Decker for factoring a non-monic polynomial by lifting mod p^k and taking principal parts, worked through on f = 15x^2 + x - 2 to the answer 'principal part: 5x+2, 3x-1'. factor(15*x^2+x-2) over ZZ[x] returns (3x - 1)(5x + 2) -- the recipe's own answer, computed by factory, which does the Hensel lifting internally. The note records a technique rather than a defect, and the capability it is a technique for works. The sibling 1-factoring-library, settled fixed earlier, records that FLINT and factory are both hard dependencies now

both halves hold where they can. 'When it's possible, ringmaps should be implemented as promotion': over a genuine tower, zzR = QQ[a] and zzS = zzR[b], promote(a^2, zzS) and map(zzS,zzR)(a^2) compare ==, so where the map is the canonical inclusion the two agree. 'Conversely, for any ring map, there should be something like lift': lift back along that inclusion returns a^2. Along a map that is not an inclusion -- a |-> c^3 into QQ[c] -- lift fails, as it must, since recovering a preimage there is a computation rather than a coercion, and preimage(RingMap, Ideal) is the method for it. Recorded fixed on the observable rather than on the implementation: whether map literally dispatches to promote internally I did not check, and the file's sentence is a suggestion about how to implement rather than a claim that anything is wrong. A first attempt at this measurement failed to ring shadowing -- after zzS = QQ[a,b] the global a belongs to zzS, so the map could not be applied to it -- and had to be redone with zzR_0

the need is met; neither mechanism it proposes was built. Dan asks for two things -- 'perhaps it is time for gb to return the inverse of the change matrix, too, same for the syzygy matrix', and 'return the map as a Matrix with the pre-computed inverse cached inside ... invert it at zero cost' -- and neither exists: getChangeMatrix at gb.m2:199 returns one matrix from rawGBChangeOfBasis, there is no inverse and no syzygy-matrix inverse, and no Matrix carries a cached inverse. Recorded fixed on the need, with the two unbuilt proposals named here so the record is not misread

'make \m2{}, a tex macro' -- prompted by Justin Walker describing SAGE's \sage{}, and by Dan's own filter living in a separate M2-tex repository rather than in the tree. MergeTeX is a distributed package now, headline 'Run Macaulay2 code inside a LaTeX file', added by d3d97784d1 (2022-03-30). It parses a LaTeX file for Macaulay2 code inside \begin{lstlisting}[language=Macaulay2] blocks or pulled from an external file, runs it, and writes a new file with the output substituted, replacing \macoutput{n} with the nth output; mergeTeXFile acts idempotently, and MergeTeX/lst-Macaulay2.tex ships the listings language definition. Different spelling from \m2{} and from the <<<...>>> brackets the file's own filter used, same need -- writing a paper with M2 code and its results displayed inline -- and in the distribution rather than beside it

half fixed, and the live half belongs with its sibling. one sentence to Mike -- 'Have you heard whether this Seysen algorithm is better than LLL?' -- with a link to a thesis chapter, and no reply in the file. 'An idle question for an idle moment: Given a ZZ[x,y]-module, how do we compute the primes of ZZ over which it is not flat?' -- the file's own framing, addressed to Mike, with a worked example rather than a request. Nothing provides it: there is no isFlat for modules anywhere in Core or the distributed packages, the only isFlat-shaped names being isFlatPolynomialRing in Elimination.m2, MinimalPrimes/quickGB.m2 and OldChainComplexes/res.m2, which test whether a ring is a polynomial ring over a field or ZZ and are unrelated. The method the example illustrates still works -- base change a resolution along ZZ[x,y] -> ZZ/p[t,u] and look at homology, which is nonzero in degree 1 for p = 2 in his example -- but getting the set of bad primes without knowing which to try is the actual question, and that is mathematics (Fitting ideals, generic freeness) rather than a missing convenience function. No consumer in twenty years

the file asks a question and both halves of it check out. Its observation first: repeatedly applying 'gens gb transpose' to a random 2x4 matrix over QQ[x,y,z, MonomialOrder => Position => Up] stabilizes -- from step 7 onward each matrix is === to the one two steps before, alternating between 23x6 and 6x23, which is exactly 'things seem to stabilize, and alternate matrices are ==='. Then the question, 'Is gb now giving a well-defined result that depends only on the submodule?': measured by presenting one submodule two ways, a 2x2 matrix I and I | I*matrix{{1,1},{0,1}} with redundant generators, where image I == image J holds. gens gb of the two are not merely == but ===, the identical object, so the answer does not depend on the presentation. Note the procedure here is the same one 2-Smith-normal-form wondered about and that became smithNormalForm two days after that file was written

split into 11 asks in asks.tsv, nothing filed. Correcting the earlier note on this row, which said ten: the two cocoa-lib tricks are separate asks, giving eleven across lines 3-26. Noro's algorithm is the closest thing to a candidate and is held for want of evidence rather than because it exists: GB over a number field works via toField, verified on QQ[i]/(i^2+1) where gb ideal(x^2+1,x*y-i) gives x-iy and y^2-1 and a cyclic-roots system returns at once, but no measurement shows the general path is deficient there, so a request to adopt a specific algorithm has nothing to point at. Three false leads worth recording: I claimed no renderer targets TeXmacs, having found only the --texmacs session flag in startup.m2.in without looking for a renderer, and Doug corrected it; e/f4/moninfo.hpp:51's mask looks like the cocoa divisibility mask but is overflow detection in check_monomial, testing the 0x10000000 guard bit; and the Noro hits in Chordal.m2 and MultiGradedRationalMap.m2 are substring noise, lMonoRows containing 'noRo'. not a note but a 126-line svn diff against M2/Macaulay2/d/M2mem.c at revision 15728, adding an x86_64-only framepointer macro (inline asm reading %rbp), a pbacktrace frame walker, and a framecheck() called from getmem, freemem, freememlen, getmem_clear and getmoremem_atomic. Never applied -- framepointer, framecheck and pbacktrace match nothing in the tree -- and it cannot be: M2mem.c is 103 lines now with different guards, MEMDEBUG and NDEBUG around trapchk rather than DEBUG. The idea has no merit left either, which was checked rather than assumed. It detects corruption only by crashing, since framecheck walks the chain until NULL or segfault and reports nothing about what wrote where; it costs a full stack walk on every allocation in an interpreter that allocates continuously, which may be why Dan wrapped the body in #if 0 before saving it; and it is x86_64 asm, so it cannot run where M2's crashes actually are -- of 27 open crash and segfault issues, #1900 and #1903 are armhf, #1746 mipsel and ppc64, #2181 and #2242 ppc64. -fomit-frame-pointer at -O2 means %rbp is not a chain unless forced, and d/CMakeLists.txt:223 already carries a FIXME about __builtin_frame_address, the portable spelling, causing trouble in M2lib.c. Recorded but not filed: M2 has no sanitizer option in autotools or CMake, so there is no supported build with memory-error detection
