all four of its round-trips pass once two renamed API spellings are fixed. 51 lines whose first line asks that the tests be moved into EngineTests.m2 'once ARing's are really ready'. Each block builds a raw mutable matrix, copies it, inserts three columns at position 2 and four rows at position 1, deletes them again, and asserts the result equals the copy; the rings are rawARingZZFlint(), ZZp(101,"Choose"=>"FLINT"), and a polynomial ring, followed by a small rawSolve test. Run as written it stops immediately on 'encountered an unknown key or option: Choose'. Two things were renamed: the option is Strategy now, not "Choose", and the values are capitalised rather than all-caps -- ZZp accepts "Flint", "Ffpack" and "Aring" and rejects "FLINT", "FFPACK" and "ARING". With those corrected every round-trip passes: rawARingZZFlint, ZZp Strategy=>"Flint", ZZp Strategy=>"Ffpack" and the polynomial ring all satisfy M == N. So the insert and delete operations the file was written to check are sound. Note that the determinant of a ZZFlint matrix, which test-flint.m2 reaches, is a different matter -- see that row. Nothing to file.

a live segfault with heap corruption, known since 2014 and recorded nowhere findable. 256 lines exercising the FLINT engine rings: rawARingZZFlint arithmetic on big integers, raw mutable matrices, rank, multiplication and determinants, with the later two thirds wrapped in TEST /// blocks that only register. Run as written it segfaults, and the crash reduces to two lines -- debug Core then rawLinAlgDeterminant raw mutableMatrix matrix(ZZFlint, {{1,0},{0,1}}) -- with a stack going fmpz_mat_det_divisor, fmpz_mat_solve_dixon, fmpz_mat_solve_bound, fmpz_sqrtrem, __gmpz_sqrtrem, __gmpn_sqrtrem, plus 'Fatal glibc error: malloc.c:2599 (sysmalloc): assertion failed', so it corrupts the heap rather than merely faulting. The trigger is a zero entry: {{1,1},{1,2}} gives 1, {{0}} gives 0, and a zero-free 3x3 gives the right 477133, while {{1,0},{0,1}}, {{5,0},{0,5}}, {{1,2},{3,0}} and that same 3x3 with one entry changed to 0 all crash -- one entry is the whole difference between 482494 and a segfault. It is known: EngineTests.m2:205-207 has ringsPID with "ZZFlint" commented out, and the ZZFlint block at LinearAlgebra.Test.FLINT.m2:200-206 is a bare /// string rather than TEST /// so testDeterminant never runs on it, both done by 50058c0907 (Mike Stillman, 2014-06-09) whose message reads 'Changes to tests. One test is still failing: crashing bug.' Twelve years on, nothing in the tracker mentions ZZFlint or QQFlint, so that commit message and two commented-out lines are the entire record. Filed per Doug's call combining the report with a fix-or-remove ask: ZZFlint is unexported and undocumented, living as ZZFlintRing in m2/flint.m2:6-13, so either it gets fixed and its ready-written tests re-enabled or it should be removed, since a half-present ring that corrupts the heap is worse than none; QQFlint is in the same state, marked 'not working yet' at EngineTests.m2:201 with testRank annotated FAILS in its own inert block. Searched titles for ZZFlint, QQFlint, flint, determinant, rawLinAlgDeterminant, fmpz, sqrtrem, heap, malloc, glibc and linear algebra, bodies for ZZFlint, and comments for ZZFlint, QQFlint, rawLinAlgDeterminant and fmpz_mat_det_divisor; #487 with its fix #2546 and test #3304 is the M2-level det and minors segfault over polynomial rings, and #1136 names rawLinAlgDeterminant but over ZZ/2[a..d] and reports a wrong answer rather than a crash.

a performance wish over ZZ with no target, and the difficulty is the ring rather than anything specific to this computation. 21 lines whose first is the entire claim: 'It would be nice if this computation could be made faster. 25 May 2013.' The computation is gens gb of a three-generator ideal in ZZ[y,x] under Lex with coefficients up to 93 million and degrees to 11; the rest of the file is the author working the coefficient arithmetic by hand -- gcdCoefficients of the lead coefficients, forming F + 2*y*G and 4*F + y*G and 15*F + 4*y*G, taking gcds of their lead coefficients, and a bare gcd(707472, 832320) at the end. So it is a study of coefficient growth, not a bug report: nothing is asserted and no answer is called wrong. One bounded run then a verdict, per the standing rule: gens gb over ZZ with Lex did not finish in 900 sec. The comparison is what settles it -- the same three generators give a 5-element basis instantly over QQ with GRevLex, instantly over QQ with Lex, and instantly over ZZ/32003 with Lex, while over ZZ neither GRevLex nor Lex finishes, GRevLex failing to return inside 100 sec. So the order is not the obstacle and the coefficients are not the obstacle over a field; it is Groebner bases over a PID, where the basis has to track coefficient information a field computation never sees, and that is the acknowledged-hard case rather than a defect. Contemporaneous with the ZZ Groebner correctness bugs triaged in the previous batch -- #146 from 2014 and #242, #243, #244 and #316 from 2015, all now verified fixed -- so this file is the performance half of the same push, and that half remains open in the ordinary sense that ZZ is hard. Nothing to file.

not a leak: the memory is reclaimable, and an explicit collectGarbage flattens it completely. 14 lines probing mutable matrix memory over ZZFlint -- build a 100x100 matrix of entries near 2^100, then transpose it 2000 times with a collectGarbage inside the loop, then 2000 times without, then 100 rounds of building a fresh matrix, filling it and squaring it. Measured peak RSS at N=100 against N=2000: transposing without collectGarbage grows 181.9 to 1243.1 MB, about 0.56 MB per iteration, but with collectGarbage in the loop it is 125.8 then 126.0 MB, flat over 2000 iterations, so nothing is retained and the growth is deferred collection -- which is exactly what the file's own two-loop structure was built to distinguish, so it answers itself. The multiply loop grows 219.7 to 743.8 MB, the same story on a bigger allocation. Worth recording next to git-468-memory-leak.m2, whose #488 loop I measured the same way in this batch: there the growth survives collectGarbage unchanged, 355.6 to 688.5 MB with it against 355.9 to 686.3 without, so that one is real retention while this one is not. Same technique, opposite outcomes, which is what makes either conclusion trustworthy. Nothing to file.

the function is right; the file's assertions are stale by two fields. 29 lines from 15 April 2013 whose second line asks that it be moved into Macaulay2Doc/test after 1.6 was released, which never happened. It checks monomialOrderMatrix against expected values for eight monomial orders. Run as written it stops at the first assert. The reason is not a wrong answer: in all three assert-bearing cases the matrix and the order type come out exactly as expected -- (matrix{{1,2,3,4}}, Lex) for Weights plus Lex=>4, the three-row matrix with RevLex for the two-Weights case, and the five-row matrix with RevLex for Weights plus 3 plus 1 -- but the return value now carries two more components, Position => Up and ComponentBefore => -1, so a 4-tuple is being compared against a 2-tuple. The remaining five orders in the file only print, and they print sensible matrices, including the Eliminate 4 case in ten variables with mixed degrees. So monomialOrderMatrix has been extended, not broken, and updating the expected tuples is all that stands between this file and passing. Nothing to file.

the assertion fails because of what the file itself does two lines earlier, not because of a defect. 46 lines headed 'Test of reducing a matrix, or a resolution, via pivots': resolve ideal(a*b*c-d*f, a^2*e^2-b*c, a*d*f-b*c*e^2) over ZZ/32003[a..f], make the three differentials mutable, call rawReduceByPivots on each, then a long hand-worked sequence of columnSwap, rowSwap, columnAdd and rowAdd to prune the resolution, ending in submatrices assembled into a chainComplex. Run as written it stops at the one assert, (matrix M2)*(matrix M3) == 0. That is the file's own doing: rawReduceByPivots works -- it takes M3 from 16 nonzero entries to 7 -- but applying it to M2 and M3 independently breaks the complex property, and I checked both halves, the composite being zero before any reduction and nonzero after reducing the two independently. Applying the file's swaps to unreduced differentials makes the same assert pass. The file anticipates this: the comment at line 28 reads 'now work on M2 (but make changes to M3 and M1 as needed)', so the compensating operations on neighbouring maps are the point of the exercise and the assert simply sits before them. This is someone working out a pruning procedure by hand, and the procedure now exists as the shipped pruneComplex. Nothing to file.

a SortStrategy scratchpad whose first eight lines correct an issue I filed earlier in this triage. 200 lines the author describes as 'my scratch area for experimentation... checked in because I use it on several machines': resolutions of a Gorenstein ideal in seven variables under each of Strategy 0 through 3 with Strategy 2 marked 'very bad!', then a long series of res calls varying SortStrategy, a COMPARE helper assembling the sort-type bits, and a 3x3 commuting-matrices example. Its stated wish, line 10, is to compute the graded Betti numbers of a free resolution without minimalizing it, which is now served by res(..., Strategy=>Nonminimal) together with betti, and minimalBetti for the other direction. What matters is the table at the top decoding the SortStrategy bits, because it includes '2^13 -- do_by_level=1 (returns non-minimal res)'. #4636, which I filed from 5-res-options.m2, presented bit 13's non-minimal return as a defect; this shows the author knew it did that and recorded it as the flag's nature, so that half is better read as an undocumented internal flag than as a bug, and I have said so in a comment there rather than leave the overstatement standing. The crash half is untouched: the same table lists 2^15 as auto_reduce = 2 and 2^14+2^15 as auto_reduce = 3 with no hint that either fails, and those are precisely the values that segfault in res2_poly::remove. The table also asks whether 2^17 is 'also non-minimal?' -- measured, it is not, giving the same minimal basis as SortStrategy 0 -- and calls 2^13+2^18 'level strip', matching the deliberate non-minimal marking in 5-res-options.m2. Together with the named constants at the top of 5-res-bench.m2 this is one of only two decodings of those bits outside res-a0.hpp. Nothing further to file.

a quasi-homogeneity question posed to Singular, with the M2 side stopping at `end`. 35 lines: over ZZ/32003[a..f] it sets z = ae-bd, y = -af+cd, x = bf-ce, then a degree-nine form F in x, y and z, and J = ideal jacobian ideal F. That is all M2 does -- `end` is line 10 -- and it makes no claim. The rest is a Singular session over the same ring with the weighted order ws(3,1,-1,4,2,0), computing jacob(F) and then qhweight(j), which returns 3,1,-1,4,2,0: Singular recovering the weights under which the ideal is quasi-homogeneous. So the implied wish is an M2 equivalent of qhweight, a function that finds a weight vector making a given ideal quasi-homogeneous, and nothing in the file asserts that M2 gets anything wrong. Left as a wish rather than a request: the file never states it, and reading a feature request out of a Singular transcript would be putting words in the author's mouth. Nothing to file.
